VibePascal v59 -- arm-linux NATIVE compiler (32-bit ARM, ARMHF/EABIHF; a 32-bit
Raspberry Pi OS is the target this exists for).  A COM interface function-result
temp is released at the end of its statement.
Source commit: 5c89c538b8fb1f00c83fb5cabd9260f6e71caba4
Compiler commits: 55e687f581 (GOD, the mechanism) + 5c89c538b8 (statement ownership, escape sweep, every statement list)
Parent release for THIS target: v58 (dedf242c69)
Built: 2026-09-17, cross-built on x86_64-linux via a freshly bootstrapped
       compiler/ppcrossarm (md5 6236206b913843c9d49f84d7b5edbe70, itself built from a
       CLEAN unit tree by the v59 native ppcx64, md5 12220bfd5b3a9b1ee6db7b68297f0844),
       -dFPC_ARMHF at BOTH stages, BINUTILSPREFIX=arm-linux-gnueabihf-;
       241 units compiled for this binary from a clean compiler/arm/units/arm-linux
Binary: bin/ppcarm  md5 c2aeb6f1abc246b517d7c9974361c3bb
                    sha256 66a9febf67a63565437ded067cf4f35c046d70bd2b3a263ce44ccf2821c78b32
                    5670904 bytes, ELF 32-bit ARM EABI5, statically linked, stripped

ABI: ARMHF (EABIHF), hard float.  readelf reports flags 0x5000400, "Version5
EABI, hard-float ABI".  The compiler tree defaults to FPC_ARMEL, so this build
passes -dFPC_ARMHF explicitly; unchanged since v56.  It is NOT compatible with
an armel (soft-float) system.

BIN-ONLY, AND THE UNITS ARE NOT OPTIONAL.  This tarball contains the compiler and
nothing else.  Pair it with vibepascal-v54-arm-linux-units-full.tar.gz, which
sits beside it in this directory (see UNITS.txt), stays valid, and is still
REQUIRED -- this is a refresh of an install, not a standalone one.

WHAT CHANGED IN v59 -- A COM INTERFACE TEMP DIES WITH ITS STATEMENT
  A function that returns a COM interface, called where its result is never
  stored in a variable ("Giver.Need.o.DoWork;"), leaves the reference in a
  hidden temp.  Up to v58 that temp was released only when the ROUTINE exited
  (or when the compiler happened to recycle the slot), so the object stayed
  checked out long past its line -- a holder that should have handed its object
  back at the semicolon kept it until the end of the procedure.  v59 releases it
  at the end of the source statement that produced it, the way Delphi does.

  Two commits carry it, and the second one is why the first did not ship alone:

    55e687f581  (GOD, 2026-09-16)  the mechanism.  A temp knows it holds a COM
                interface (tgobj), a slot still holding one is never recycled
                under a second result in the same statement, and tcgblocknode
                releases the statement's temps after every statement of a
                begin..end block.

    5c89c538b8  (Otto, 2026-09-17)  three holes measured on that build with
                the two matrices added in tests/test/ (tintfstmttemp1.pp, 32
                corners; tintfstmttemp2.pp, 28 corners), closed before anything
                shipped:
                  * a statement nested inside another -- the body of a
                    with/if/while/case whose EXPRESSION produced the temp --
                    released its parent's temp.  `with Giver.Need.o do begin
                    A; B end` ran B on a freed object (measured: the owner's
                    refcount hit zero after A).  Each temp now records which
                    source statement allocated it and a statement releases
                    only its own, never an enclosing one's.
                  * exit, break, continue, goto and raise LEAKED the temp for
                    good: the routine-exit sweep had been trimmed to skip
                    temps whose statement-end release existed, and those
                    escapes never reach that release.  Measured: every one of
                    them leaked exactly one object.  The sweep covers every
                    managed temp again; a slot that was already released is
                    nil and costs one compare, one that was abandoned is
                    released at routine exit, and nothing is released twice.
                  * repeat..until bodies, try/finally/except bodies and
                    case-else lists kept the old routine-exit lifetime, because
                    only begin..end had been marked as a source statement list.

  What does NOT change: an interface stored in a variable, field, array or
  Result lives exactly as long as it always did.  Two results used in one
  statement are both alive until that statement ends.  A temp produced by an
  if/while condition, a case selector or a with expression stays alive through
  the branch, the loop body or the with block and is released when that
  statement ends.

  COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  No RTL change, no package change, no PPU FORMAT change
  (the unit files' own header/version are untouched), so every existing unit
  set for this target stays valid and does not need rebuilding.  Code compiled
  by v59 simply releases these temps sooner.

HOW THE FIX WAS PROVEN, ON THE SOURCE EVERY TARGET IS BUILT FROM
  * tests/test/tintfstmttemp1.pp and tintfstmttemp2.pp, 60 self-checking
    corners in all (free proc, method, nested proc, main body, if/for/while/
    repeat/with bodies, two temps in one statement, a temp passed as a
    parameter, a stored interface, exit/break/continue/goto/raise mid-
    statement, a nested block under a with/if/while/case temp, try/finally/
    except/on/case-else bodies, an unentered block, and destroyed == created
    at the end): 60/60 on this source at -O- and -O2.  The same programs score
    35 failures on v58 (everything released at routine exit, nothing leaked,
    nothing freed early) and 31 on the 55e687f581 build (3 leaked objects, 4
    use-after-free corners, 6 statement lists left on the old lifetime) -- so
    the harness fails in both directions and a pass means something.
  * 1983-test corpus A/B against the PUBLISHED v58 x86_64-linux compiler:
    1983 SAME, 0 DIFF (compile status and run exit code per test).
  * self-host fixpoint on x86_64-linux: stage 2 == stage 3 byte-identical.
  * dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh, the v57/v58 reader fixes are still in:
    25/25 offsets clean on x86_64-linux, i386-linux, aarch64-linux and
    arm-linux with the host-executable compilers.
  * dist/unit-set-loadcheck.sh: x86_64-linux 147/147, i386-linux 146/146,
    aarch64-linux 144/144, arm-linux 143/143 packages load clean, zero
    recompiles.

VERIFIED ON THESE EXACT BYTES
  * EXECUTION, not inspection.  Under qemu-arm-static this binary reports
    3.3.1 / arm, compiled both lifetime matrices against the tree's arm-linux
    units (-XParm-linux-gnueabihf- for the host cross binutils), and the
    products RAN under qemu: tintfstmttemp1 checks=32 fails=0,
    tintfstmttemp2 checks=28 fails=0 created=27 destroyed=27 live=0.
  * dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh ppcarm arm-linux, against the real
    packages/aspell/units/arm-linux/aspelldyn.ppu: 25/25 offsets clean,
    0 problems, exit 0, with the gate's cap raised to 8 GB
    (TRUNCCHECK_VMCAP_KB=8388608).  Under the gate's DEFAULT 1 GB cap a
    32-bit guest cannot start at all under qemu-user binfmt -- "Unable to
    find a guest_base to satisfy all guest address mapping requirements
    00000000-ffffffff" -- and the gate then scores 24/25 with "the compiler
    rejects a GOOD unit".  That is the emulator, not the compiler: the
    published v58 ppcarm scores exactly the same 24/25 under the default cap
    and 25/25 under the raised one, measured today.  The arm CROSS compiler
    built from this same source scores 25/25 under the default cap.
  * dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh exercises this tarball end to end and checks the
    md5 above against the bytes it unpacks.

NOT PROVEN HERE, AND SAID PLAINLY: qemu-user is an emulator.  It runs the real
shipped bytes and real ARM instruction encodings, so codegen and RTL defects DO
surface -- but it is not a Raspberry Pi.  NOBODY HAS RUN ANY VIBEPASCAL RELEASE
ON PHYSICAL ARM SILICON.  Do not quote a pass here as a hardware sign-off.
